transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Rossi (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Verdant Lattice - Head of Platform), Tomas Ortega (Verdant - Lead SA), Evelyn Park (Verdant - Partnerships)

Summary:
Quick partner discovery between Redwood and Verdant Lattice to understand onramp requirements for SI-led GPU integrations, clarify network/VPC constraints, and scope a pilot to validate throughput and cost targets. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Verdant's current hybrid deployment model and partner reseller motion
- Technical constraints: VPC peering, private deployments, certs/KMS
- Performance goals & sample workload characteristics
- Commercial alignment: reseller discounts, co-sell credits, pilot SOW

Action items (recap in call):
- SE benchmark plan; customer to share perf targets; AE to share commercial framework

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to chat through a possible onramp flow with Verdant Lattice. can you give us a quick overview of what you guys are trying to achieve?
[00:12] Priya Nair: yeah thanks Maya. sure. so Verdant Lattice is an SI focusing on edge and regulated verticals, we resell a managed infra + integration package to about 25 enterprise clients. our customers are asking for a tighter path to LLM inference — ideally something we can white-label and support on-prem or in their VPCs.
[00:28] Tomas Ortega: to add -- our typical deployment is hybrid, we run orchestration in our cloud but push inference into customer data centers for residency and latency. so we need a partner that supports both hosted and private models.
[00:40] Luca Rossi: okay makes sense. do you currently run any LLMs yourself or rely on public endpoints?
[00:45] Priya Nair: we have some internal inference on pre-baked transformer models using a mix of in-house GPU clusters and a few cloud partners — mostly proof-of-concepts. right now cost and unpredictable latency are the two blockers.
[00:57] Maya Chen: yeah totally. from Redwood's side we do hosted API, dedicated pools, and private VPC/on-prem installs. curious about the scale — how big are you thinking for a pilot?
[01:08] Tomas Ortega: pilot scope would be 2-4 client integrations, each with bursty traffic patterns. typical peak qps per client ~50 to 200, but lots of short seq generation requests. average context length about 256 tokens, sometimes 1024 for a few use cases.
[01:26] Evelyn Park: also important: some clients require FIPS-validated crypto and KMS integration with their HSMs.
[01:33] Luca Rossi: okay that helps. so workload profile: short, bursty, medium context. that maps well to our autoscaling/dedicated pools with prefix caching to reduce cost. for the HSM integration — we do KMS connectors and can support customer-managed keys in Private. there can be some nuance with FIPS though, we should flag that.
[01:52] Priya Nair: yep we'll need that spelled out. security is a gating factor for a few of our customers. SOC2 and ISO27001 are table stakes too.
[02:02] Maya Chen: we can share SOC2 and ISO artifacts. quick question on networking: do you prefer VPC peering or private link style connections? and are your deployments multi-tenant at your end or fully isolated per customer?
[02:16] Tomas Ortega: preference depends on customer. for large financials we do VPC peering with strict firewall rules, for mid-market it's usually private link. we provision dedicated subnets per customer for the inference nodes — level of isolation is pretty high.
[02:29] Luca Rossi: good. Redwood Private supports both: we can do direct peering, private link, or an on-prem package behind their firewall. but we need to understand performance target and what latency SLO customers expect.
[02:40] Priya Nair: targets vary: the low-latency use case wants p50 < 80ms for 256-token responses. others are fine with p95 under 500ms. cost sensitivity also varies — some clients will pay for low latency, others want minimal cost.
[02:57] Maya Chen: got it. regarding model choices, are you planning to host open models or bring-your-own-model?
[03:03] Tomas Ortega: a mix. some clients want open models tuned by Verdant, others want to run vendor-supplied LLMs. we need the runtime to be flexible on model variants and quantization.
[03:14] Luca Rossi: that's standard. our runtime supports fp16 and int8 quantization paths, and can route requests to different model variants based on policy. there can be slight quality/cost tradeoffs when using aggressive quant.
[03:26] Evelyn Park: aptitude question: how invasive is the Private install? do you need kernel-level hooks or anything that makes it difficult for our ops team to review?
[03:36] Maya Chen: no kernel hooks. Private is packaged as a customer-managed control plane + agent for the inference nodes; installs are containerized and our operations team has a documented playbook. but some customers insist on air-gapped installs which take additional steps.
[03:51] Tomas Ortega: hmm air-gapped is tricky for a few of our clients. do you have an offline package or a mirror repo approach?
[03:59] Luca Rossi: we have an on-prem bundle designed for air-gapped environments. it requires a one-time manual transfer of artifacts and a small footprint installer. we usually run a short validation test with the client's auditors.
[04:10] Priya Nair: that's promising. shifting to commercial: Verdant often takes a reseller margin and sometimes handles first-line support. do you have a partner discount tier or a channel program?
[04:21] Maya Chen: yes we do have a partner program with tiered discounts based on committed committed reserved capacity or monthly ARR. we also do co-sell credits for strategic deals. we can share a partner one-pager after the call.
[04:34] Evelyn Park: great. for pilots we also need to negotiate how support handoff will work — Verdant would prefer to own triage initially, escalate to Redwood for platform bugs.
[04:44] Luca Rossi: fine — we usually set up a joint-support playbook for pilots: Verdant does first-touch, Redwood SEs are on-call for infra/bug escalations. we'll capture that in the SOW.
[04:55] Tomas Ortega: on the technical checklist, we need to run a baseline: latency and throughput across 1) hosted 2) dedicated pool 3) private VPC, using our sample workload. how invasive would that test be?
[05:07] Luca Rossi: not invasive — we can spin a dedicated pool in our staging infra and run a 48-hour baseline with your trace workload. for private VPC tests we'd need connectivity and a small node footprint on your side.
[05:19] Priya Nair: timeline? we have a few customers in pilot windows mid-Oct. can we do a baseline next week?
[05:25] Maya Chen: realistic schedule depends on paperwork and access. SE-led baseline could start in 7-10 days if we get perf targets and keys.
[05:34] Evelyn Park: paperwork is a blocker. procurement will want an initial MSA — do you have a partner MSA template?
[05:40] Maya Chen: we have a partner-friendly MSA and a reseller addendum. I'll circulate that after the call.
[05:47] Tomas Ortega: also need to align on telemetry and observability — our customers rarely accept opaque models. can we expose traces and token-level cost per call?
[05:57] Luca Rossi: yes Redwood Console exposes per-route token costs, latency breakdowns, and traces. for Private installs we can push logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and also provide a read-only console if desired.
[06:10] Priya Nair: perfect. on legal/security again — a couple of customers want contractual language for encryption at rest and in transit and audit log retention. are you flexible on retention windows?
[06:21] Maya Chen: we can support configurable retention; for hosted we have 30/90/365 day plans, Private you control retention. for encryption we use TLS1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest; support customer-managed keys in Private.
[06:36] Tomas Ortega: okay good. small nit: do you support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for RBAC?
[06:42] Luca Rossi: yes SAML SSO and SCIM supported for RBAC across Console.
[06:47] Evelyn Park: back to the onramp pattern — Verdant typically bundles the infra + integration and wants an integration kit: terraform modules, helm charts, and a sample operator manifest. do you provide that?
[06:59] Maya Chen: we have Terraform + Helm templates and a documented operator manifest for Private installs and dedicated pools. we'll put those in a partner repo.
[07:08] Tomas Ortega: excellent. for the pilot we'll need an infra manifest and minimum node sizes. what's the minimum GPU configuration you recommend for 256-token, p50 ~80ms?
[07:20] Luca Rossi: depends on model family. for modern open LLMs quantized to int8, a single A10 or A100sized vGPU equivalent could hit those numbers at modest qps; for more headroom we'd recommend an A100-80GB class. we'll include exact recommendations in the benchmark plan.
[07:35] Priya Nair: cost question — do you publish cost per token metrics for different pool types? some of our clients want line-of-sight to unit economics.
[07:43] Maya Chen: yes we have token-level cost breakdowns in Console and an Optimize toolkit that suggests batching/quantization to reduce unit cost. we can run your workload and estimate cost delta across hosted vs private.
[07:57] Tomas Ortega: one more technical thing — model routing. can we create policies that route based on customer tier or region?
[08:04] Luca Rossi: yes routing policies are policy-driven: latency-first, cost-first, or region-priority. you can pin model versions per-customer.
[08:12] Priya Nair: ok good. now to risk/objections — a few clients push back on vendor lock-in and portability. how easy is it to move inference images elsewhere?
[08:22] Maya Chen: we try to avoid lock-in by using standard containers and by letting customers export model weights and caches. the orchestration layer is opinionated but exportable; we can document migration steps.
[08:34] Tomas Ortega: that's reassuring. shifting to pilot SOW — what would you include as success criteria?
[08:40] Luca Rossi: I would propose: 1) validated latency SLOs for specified payloads, 2) cost per 1M tokens within agreed band vs current baseline, 3) secure connectivity and KMS integration validated by customer security team, 4) operator playbook and runbook handed to Verdant.
[08:57] Evelyn Park: that sounds right. can we get a template for the SOW?
[09:01] Maya Chen: yes will attach a pilot SOW template.
[09:05] Priya Nair: timeline reiteration — our customers' pilot windows mid-Oct; we'd prefer Redwood to start the bench in the next two weeks so we can present results by mid-Oct.
[09:14] Maya Chen: we'll try — Luca will draft a benchmark/infra plan today and circulate.
[09:19] Luca Rossi: yep I'll put together a 48-hour baseline plan listing test harness and manifests. I might ping Tomas for sample traces.
[09:26] Tomas Ortega: I'll share traces and a small synthetic generator.
[09:29] Evelyn Park: while we're on sharing, can Redwood share an example partner case study or reference?
[09:34] Maya Chen: we have a reference with a fintech partner that did a dedicated deployment and saw 3x cost reduction using caching+quantization. I'll send that link.
[09:43] Priya Nair: last compliance note — do you allow customer audits for Private installs?
[09:48] Luca Rossi: yes for Private we support onsite or remote audits and provide necessary artifacts.
[09:53] Maya Chen: ok I think we're near time. quick recap of next steps?
[09:57] Priya Nair: Verdant: share performance targets and sample traces (Tomas).
[10:00] Tomas Ortega: will do by EOD tomorrow.
[10:03] Maya Chen: Redwood: Luca to produce benchmark plan by 2026-09-10; Maya to circulate partner MSA and channel one-pager; SE/AE to schedule follow-up in two weeks.
[10:13] Evelyn Park: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[10:16] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the repo link. bye.

End of meeting.
